correctness.rationale: KKT uniquely identifies clipped radial scaling. Each smooth active stratum yields derivative s^{-1}(I-uu^T) on free coordinates. Its exact ell_infty row norm is optimized with Cauchy–Schwarz and scalar clamping to a provably feasible interval. Continuity and generic-segment integration give the global upper bound; explicit strictly feasible capped-face inputs as s decreases to 1 give matching two-input lower bounds. Algebra proves the n=13 clipped-face strict inequality and radius threshold jump. Independent standard-library computation passed 2,951 supplementary checks but is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The intersection of amplitude box constraints and Euclidean energy constraints is a natural full family of convex feasibility sets. Exact coordinatewise robustness is needed for individual-entry error bounds; one saturated coordinate can outrank the ball-only stratum (n=13), and the optimal conditioning jumps when the energy constraint becomes redundant, despite continuity of sets. The all-dimensional active-face formula is not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine renaming of ball-only clipping.
